scope: Adversarial refresh of six Japan–Korea–Singapore routes; national acceptance authority versus portable evidence. Four proposed designs, no score changes. Existing route data and report read first. Cutoff 2026-10-31; Geneva checkpoint 2027-06-21/22. Supplier submissions are attributed positions, not established facts or consent.

routes.headline: A real platform approval gate exists, but independent assurance and supplier disclosure cannot be inferred from it.

newEvidence.claim: FACT: DS-920 §6.3.3 includes diverse/independent internal and external testing, including red teaming, as example methods before release. It does not make an external independent certificate universally compulsory.

ATTRIBUTED SUPPLIER POSITION / OFFICIAL RESPONSE: Graffer and Rakuten object that downstream API providers cannot disclose upstream training data/algorithms. The agency says contract-checklist item 8 is not a uniform disclosure requirement; scope depends on agreement and reasonableness.
newEvidence.locator: physical p69, printed p68, contract checklist item 8

newEvidence.claim: FACT: The Gen-nai standard's second review is by another Gen-nai developer, alongside an authorised official's approval. The standard also explicitly plans interchangeable components, migration testing and aggregate public usage reporting.

ATTRIBUTED SUPPLIER POSITION / OFFICIAL RESPONSE: Graffer flags unannounced upstream model changes and forced retirement. The agency retains the original wording and says important systems may require action beyond the supplier's controllable scope.

supports: A buyer-controlled production release is more concrete than a voluntary national principle.
The final government guideline covers inappropriate output, bias and expected quality as well as security; the programme need not invent an AI-risk vocabulary.
Documented migration and transparency policies provide hooks for testing substitutability and accountability.
challenges: A second in-house developer is not an external independent safety assessor.
The severe-vulnerability release prohibition is not automatically an enforceable hallucination, discrimination or catastrophic-misuse threshold.
General normative duties for government do not give every checklist example binding effect against every supplier.
More onerous disclosure could exclude integrators without obtaining upstream evidence; the supplier cannot guarantee a version it does not control.
The agency's refusal to narrow obligations for important systems means the solution is a feasible fallback or different supplier, not silently waiving evidence.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: executed Gen-nai supplier acceptance schedule, liability/termination provisions and amendment powers for the proposed exact gate.
FUTURE/UNOBSERVED: actual FY2027 final tender changes, marginal independent-testing prices and measured acceptance delay.
NOT LOCATED: a witnessed AI-safety failed-release hold, version-pinned upstream service guarantee, operational migration test or gated-token ledger.
UNMEASURED: displacement to departmental tools or offshore APIs and lost service utility.
routes.decisionTest: Select one live model/application contract and obtain its signed acceptance schedule plus release delegation. Introduce a consented synthetic leakage failure and an upstream-version-retirement scenario in staging. Require the authorised official to record hold, fallback and fresh-test decisions. Disconfirm the apparent Japan advantage if evidence cannot be obtained on time, the fallback cannot perform the required service, or the workload simply moves to an ungated service. Count successfully gated activity and utility, not access-enabled staff.

ideas.title: Version-and-fallback acceptance annex
ideas.proposal: Pilot one application-specific acceptance annex binding model endpoint/version where available, system prompt, tool permissions, retrieval snapshot and independent held-out results to the authorised release record. Treat unexpected upstream changes as a hold or pretested limited-function fallback trigger.
ideas.owner: Proposed: Digital Agency Gen-nai release authority and contracting officer, with the application owner; no commitment observed.
ideas.mechanism: Prospective procurement acceptance schedule plus the existing production-change workflow; obtain express supplier agreement wherever new supplier duties are needed.
ideas.safetyDemand: No release of the named workflow after material change until a defined leakage/unauthorised-action test passes, with a service-utility floor and documented residual risks.
ideas.verification: Witness one failed test, hold, fallback and independent retest; preserve version/environment manifest, approvals, cost and elapsed time. Failure condition: no stable identity, no feasible fallback, bypassed hold or excessive false refusals.
ideas.remedy: Hold the affected application or remove tool privileges; contractual cure/retest or rejection only if actually agreed. No claim of a global model shutdown right.
ideas.deadline: Proposed scope/authority decision 2026-12-15; staging drill by 2027-03-31; operational receipt by 2027-06-01.
dependencies: Supplier update notice or detectable version change
Fallback service and procurement officer approval
ideas.whyBetter: Tests the actual right and its substitution cost instead of assuming a policy checklist or procurement spend changes supplier behaviour.

ideas.title: Confidential evidence escrow with a public decision receipt
ideas.proposal: Offer a two-tier evidence route: restricted examiner access to necessary proprietary evidence, plus public scope, tests performed, exceptions and release/hold decisions. Require a documented evidence-gap decision instead of treating undisclosable material as either a pass or an automatic demand for all training data.
ideas.owner: Proposed: buyer, mutually accepted independent examiner and supplier; publication authority remains with the responsible public body.
ideas.mechanism: Negotiated confidentiality/access annex and procurement-neutral minimum evidence template; itemise examiner cost and test a small integrator and an upstream model supplier against the same outcomes.
ideas.safetyDemand: The examiner must reproduce the claimed mitigation for the actual deployment; unavailable evidence must narrow permitted use or trigger fallback.
ideas.verification: Compare evidence access, bidder participation, examiner hours, unresolved gaps and decision delay across the two supplier types. Publish aggregate exceptions without raw personal data or exploit details. Failure condition: examiner has no effective access, material gaps are hidden, or costs exclude otherwise capable suppliers.
ideas.remedy: Restricted deployment, documented refusal or retest; a public correction to misleading assurance claims. Contractual penalties require explicit terms.
ideas.deadline: Proposed template and permitted publication fields by 2027-01-31; first redacted decision receipt by 2027-05-31.
ideas.whyBetter: Responds to actual supplier objections while making exceptions visible and preventing a secret blanket waiver from replacing assurance.

scoreImplications.implication: Retain the distinction between strong platform readiness and unresolved independent model-assurance readiness.
scoreImplications.reason: The final guideline and release rule supply a process, not the complete proposed evidence contract.
Buyer approval is documented, but independent evidence duties, cure rights and upstream version control remain contract-specific.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not infer international or frontier-model control from national deployment scale.
scoreImplications.reason: The enforceable object is a named government workflow; substitution and bypass remain unmeasured.

routes.headline: Portable evidence is more defensible than a common approval or common contractual remedy.

newEvidence.claim: FACT: Japan's normative guideline expects procurement and contract provisions to be selected for the system and risk; it encourages additional necessary items rather than supplying a self-executing universal supplier contract.
FACT: Singapore's accreditation body explicitly does not certify tester independence or complete system safety; accreditation is scoped by risk and method.

ACCESS GAP: A candidate BSA Korean safety-notice submission was located, but direct download returned HTTP403 and the document body was not independently read. Its recommendations and legal implications are not used as evidence.

supports: A shared manifest and evidence vocabulary could reduce duplicated preparation while keeping national legal decisions separate.
Differentiating upstream and downstream obligations directly addresses supplier objections.
challenges: Common report formatting does not transfer Japanese contracting authority, Korean regulatory power or Singapore purchaser approval.
Recognition of a tester is narrower than recognition of its independence or of a deployment's safety.
A common evidence requirement could entrench large assurance vendors or exclude suppliers lacking upstream access.
Three-country spend cannot be summed without a matched application/contract pool and overlap adjustment.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: trilateral contracting adoption, mutual-recognition instrument, national acceptance owners, priced translation/retest burden or comparable purchase ledger.
UNOBSERVED: exact institutional consent; no Korean supplier position is inferred from the inaccessible candidate PDF.
routes.decisionTest: Have one purchaser per jurisdiction independently decide on the same completed evidence packet. Count additional tests, untranslated requirements, legal exceptions and review hours. Disconfirm a coalition advantage if total work/delay exceeds separate national preparation without finding additional material failures or expanding genuinely bound activity.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not collapse scientific agreement into contracting agreement.
scoreImplications.reason: Separate authorities still make risk- and contract-specific decisions.
Scoped testing competence is not demonstrated cross-border acceptance or additional protected deployments.

routes.headline: Test the whole agent and preserve utility; a safe-looking refusal or known-attack retest can mislead.

newEvidence.claim: PRIMARY RESEARCH: AgentDojo evaluates agents using tools over untrusted data, supports adaptive attacks and finds task failures even without attacks. Its version history reports an implementation bug fix, underscoring the importance of pinned harness versions.
newEvidence.locator: abstract and v3 version comments; full HTML environment/experiments sections

newEvidence.claim: OPERATOR SYNTHESIS: The assurance pilot recommends inspecting intermediate pipeline stages, particularly for agents, and calibrating LLM judges with human experts; generic model benchmarks were rarely sufficient for application tests.
newEvidence.locator: Executive summary, recommendations 2–4 and testing overview

supports: There are reusable technical methods for realistic workflow and prompt-injection testing.
A small deployment-specific gate can test real leakage rather than rely solely on model-level claims.
challenges: An agent that refuses legitimate tasks can appear safe; utility and attack success require separate endpoints.
End-of-conversation text can miss tool-side disclosure or unauthorised actions.
Adapting a defence to previously successful attacks risks overfitting.
AISI scientific competence does not itself confer the purchaser's launch authority.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: binding agency release delegation, actual blocked production release, gate-specific price/queue time and held-out leakage outcomes.
UNMEASURED: useful completed tasks lost to the safeguard and migration to other tools.
routes.decisionTest: Pin model, agent scaffold, permissions, retrieval data and evaluator versions. Run clean tasks, known attacks and independently authored held-out attacks; inspect tool traces. Compare leakage, unauthorised actions, clean-task completion, cost and time. Require an authorised failed-test hold before calling the route operational.

scoreImplications.implication: Support relevance to leakage; do not extrapolate to general catastrophic safety.
scoreImplications.reason: The technical experiment targets specific tool/data failure mechanisms.

scoreImplications.implication: Separate available test tooling from demonstrated deployment governance.
scoreImplications.reason: Realistic tests and judge calibration still require application work and owner approval.

routes.headline: A shared negative-control and execution manifest can test interoperability without pretending to harmonise law.

newEvidence.claim: PRIMARY RESEARCH: AgentDojo's dynamic/adaptive evaluation and corrected implementation demonstrate why an unversioned benchmark score is insufficient as portable evidence.
newEvidence.locator: abstract, source/version history, environment and experiment discussion

newEvidence.claim: FACT: Singapore's tester accreditation distinguishes benchmarking from red teaming and enumerates separate risk categories; it explicitly excludes an independence guarantee.

supports: There is a practical common object to standardise: execution conditions and evidence provenance.
National buyers can reuse a technical receipt without surrendering their own acceptance criteria.
challenges: The earlier bilateral experiment already shows different pipelines; this refresh does not convert its scores into a harmonised result.
A portable score may be misleading when tool permissions, language, retrieval content or evaluation judges differ.
A shared method may spread the same blind spot unless independent attacks and local context remain.
unknowns: ACCESS-LIMITED IN THIS REFRESH: the SG/KR PDF returned HTTP 403 to direct download; its exact counts remain attributed to the existing repository dossier, not a new extraction.
NOT LOCATED: Japanese acceptance, three national recognition instruments, common-cost experiment, mutual confidential-evidence terms or observed policy effect.
routes.decisionTest: Replicate the same manifest in two laboratories, then change one field at a time (tool scope, language, retrieval snapshot, judge or execution cap). Predeclare decision-disagreement and cost criteria. Reject portability for any deployment whose acceptance changes materially under an undocumented field or whose missing local tests dominate the reused work.

ideas.title: Portable test receipt with national acceptance adapters
ideas.proposal: Exchange a machine-readable manifest and trace bundle rather than a universal safety certificate. Include clean-task and attack outcomes, invalid/timeout runs, evaluator calibration, conflicts, language, permissions and residual-risk fields. Attach a distinct signed national accept/hold/retest decision.
ideas.owner: Proposed: SG/KR evaluators plus a willing Japanese application owner; each national purchaser keeps release authority.
ideas.mechanism: Voluntary technical protocol plus separate national procurement/release annexes; optional Korean incident exercise reuses traces but does not claim legal compliance.
ideas.safetyDemand: Independent replication must expose materially unsafe tool/data behaviour; unresolved portability gaps require local testing rather than automatic acceptance.
ideas.verification: Two-lab blinded replication including a deliberately defective negative control and a clean-utility control; log staff hours and disagreement. Failure condition: defect missed, cross-lab accept/hold disagreement unresolved, inaccessible traces or duplicated work erasing the expected saving.
ideas.remedy: Withdraw portability for the affected configuration and require local retesting; national authority decides any deployment hold.
ideas.deadline: Proposed schema and acceptance criteria by 2027-01-31; replication by 2027-04-30; national decision receipts by 2027-06-01.
ideas.whyBetter: Directly tests whether cooperation reduces cost or expands protection instead of assigning a coordination bonus for sharing a report.

scoreImplications.implication: Support a small technical trial, not completed recognition.
scoreImplications.reason: Reusable test methods exist while acceptance adapters are still proposed.

scoreImplications.implication: Keep remedy conditional on a national decision attachment.
scoreImplications.reason: Neither a benchmark nor accreditation is a release veto.

routes.headline: Tester accreditation is a useful competence signal, explicitly not an independence or safety guarantee.

newEvidence.claim: FACT: AIVF's accredited-tester page says accreditation does not certify testing independence or complete safety/reliability. It is limited to demonstrated risk categories and testing methods.
newEvidence.locator: introductory disclaimer and Technical Testing Competencies

newEvidence.claim: OPERATOR SYNTHESIS: The pilot's application-specific data, pipeline inspection and human calibration recommendations identify nontrivial work beyond purchasing an off-the-shelf benchmark run.

supports: A buyer can now select a provider against publicly enumerated technical competencies.
Application-focused testing is aligned with a bounded purchaser acceptance gate.
challenges: Accreditation cannot substitute for a conflict check or a signed buyer release decision.
An industry-testing programme does not itself authorise withholding launch or payment.
Bespoke data and domain experts create cost and delay; pilot participation is not proof of a cheap repeatable service.
unknowns: NOT LOCATED: actual purchaser hold clause, first blocked launch, itemised tester quote, completion-time distribution or deployment activity affected.
NOT ESTABLISHED: publication date of the live accredited-tester page; observed at cutoff only.
routes.decisionTest: For one sandbox application, independently check evaluator conflicts and competence scope, attach purchaser acceptance criteria before testing, and witness a failed-test hold. Compare quoted versus actual test effort and clean-task performance. Disconfirm readiness if no purchaser can legally or operationally hold the release despite a negative report.

ideas.title: Two-key purchaser acceptance pilot
ideas.proposal: Require a scoped, conflict-checked technical report and a separate authorised purchaser release decision. A tester cannot self-authorise launch, and a purchaser cannot describe an out-of-scope or conflicted test as independent assurance.
ideas.owner: Proposed: one participating purchaser, its application/service owner, and a competent external tester.
ideas.mechanism: Prospective statement of work and acceptance schedule with a precommitted fail/hold/retest rule, using sandbox support only where eligible.
ideas.safetyDemand: Held-out leakage and unauthorised-action tests must meet application-specific thresholds while preserving a stated useful-task completion floor.
ideas.verification: Witness an intentionally failing staging build, hold record, remediation and fresh-attack retest. Measure staff hours, delay, false refusals and gated transactions. Failure condition: conflict not mitigated, no genuine hold, thresholds changed after results or unaffordable test burden.
ideas.remedy: Withhold acceptance/launch for the affected scope; payment withholding only if lawful and in the signed contract. Permit restricted-function fallback and documented retest.
ideas.deadline: Proposed purchaser/authority selection by 2027-01-15; completed pilot and redacted receipt by 2027-05-31.
ideas.whyBetter: Supplies the missing link between a competent test service and an operationally consequential decision, without treating accreditation as certification of safety.

scoreImplications.implication: Technical supplier discovery strengthens; purchaser-governance readiness remains conditional.
scoreImplications.reason: Accreditation discloses scope and exclusions rather than certifying deployment decisions.

scoreImplications.implication: Do not infer a measured completion probability from programme target duration.
scoreImplications.reason: Use-case-specific test data and expert calibration are substantive work with no retrieved price/time distribution.
